# All Critical Target Data
## Data Manipulation
```{r}
# Load data (1 data frame)
crittarg_data <- read.csv(here("PADLD Data", "All PADLD Critical Target Mean Amps.csv"),stringsAsFactors=TRUE) # mean amplitudes for all critical targets

crittarg_data %<>%
  mutate(Mean.Amp = as.numeric(Mean.Amp),
         Channel = factor(Channel),
         Region = factor(Region, levels=c("frontal","central","parietal","occipital")),
         Hemisphere = factor(Hemisphere, levels=c("left","midline","right")),
         Priming=factor(Priming, levels=c("unprimed","primed")),
         ISI = factor(ISI,levels=c("67","317")),
         Priming.Condition = factor(Priming.Condition, levels=c("unprimed 67","primed 67","unprimed 317","primed 317")),
         Experimental.Condition = factor(Experimental.Condition),
         Stimulus.Type = factor(Stimulus.Type),
         Prime.Visibility = factor (Prime.Visibility),
         Trial.Type = factor(Trial.Type),
         Group = factor(Group), 
         gender.c = as.numeric(Gender) - 1.5,
         Detailed.Language.Status = factor(Detailed.Language.Status),
         Language.Status = factor(Language.Status,levels=c("English monolingual","English primary")),
         lang.stat.c = as.numeric(Language.Status) - 1.5,
         Bilingual.Type = factor(Bilingual.Type),
         celf5 = as.numeric(CELF5.CLS),
         celf5.c = as.numeric(scale(CELF5.CLS, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)),
         age.c = as.numeric(scale(Average.Age, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)),
         nwr.ppc.arc = asin(sqrt(as.numeric(NWR.PPC)/100)),
         nwr.ppc.arc.c = as.numeric(scale(nwr.ppc.arc, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)),
         nwr.pcc.arc = asin(sqrt(as.numeric(NWR.PCC)/100)),
         nwr.pcc.arc.c = as.numeric(scale(nwr.pcc.arc, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)),
         tills= as.numeric(TILLS.VA.Standard.Score),
         tills.c = as.numeric(scale(TILLS.VA.Standard.Score, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)),
         toni= as.numeric(TONI.Deviation.Quotient),
         toni.c = as.numeric(scale(TONI.Deviation.Quotient, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)),
         wrmt = as.numeric(WRMT.LWI.Standard.Score),
         wrmt.c = as.numeric(scale(WRMT.LWI.Standard.Score, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)),
         flanker = as.numeric(Flanker.Standard.Score),
         flanker.c = as.numeric(scale(Flanker.Standard.Score, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)),
         handedness = factor(Handedness),
         hand.c = as.numeric(handedness) - 1.5,
         pvt = factor(PVT,levels=c("50","67","83","100","> 117")))
str(crittarg_data)

# Create some data subsets
piccrittarg_data <- subset(crittarg_data,Experimental.Condition == "picture")
wordcrittarg_data <- subset(crittarg_data,Experimental.Condition == "word")
maskedpic_data <- subset(crittarg_data,Experimental.Condition == "picture" & Prime.Visibility == "masked")
maskedword_data <- subset(crittarg_data,Experimental.Condition == "word" & Prime.Visibility == "masked")
vispic_data <- subset(crittarg_data,Experimental.Condition == "picture" & Prime.Visibility == "visible")
visword_data <- subset(crittarg_data,Experimental.Condition == "word" & Prime.Visibility == "visible")
DLD_data <- subset(crittarg_data,Group == "DLD")
TL_data <- subset(crittarg_data,Group == "TL")
dldmaskedpic_data <- subset(crittarg_data,Experimental.Condition == "picture" & Prime.Visibility == "masked" & Group == "DLD")
dldmaskedword_data <- subset(crittarg_data,Experimental.Condition == "word" & Prime.Visibility == "masked" & Group == "DLD")
dldvispic_data <- subset(crittarg_data,Experimental.Condition == "picture" & Prime.Visibility == "visible" & Group == "DLD")
dldvisword_data <- subset(crittarg_data,Experimental.Condition == "word" & Prime.Visibility == "visible" & Group == "DLD")
tlmaskedpic_data <- subset(crittarg_data,Experimental.Condition == "picture" & Prime.Visibility == "masked" & Group == "TL")
tlmaskedword_data <- subset(crittarg_data,Experimental.Condition == "word" & Prime.Visibility == "masked" & Group == "TL")
tlvispic_data <- subset(crittarg_data,Experimental.Condition == "picture" & Prime.Visibility == "visible" & Group == "TL")
tlvisword_data <- subset(crittarg_data,Experimental.Condition == "word" & Prime.Visibility == "visible" & Group == "TL")

# Notes:
# Region = anteriority/posteriority; default reference level (set above) = frontal
# Hemisphere = laterality; default reference level (set above) = left
# Priming = primed vs. unprimed; default reference level (set above) = unprimed
# ISI = 67 vs. 317; default reference level (set above) = 67
# Priming Condition = Priming + ISI; default reference level (set above) = unprimed 67
# Experimental Condition = picture vs. word; default reference level = picture
# Stimulus Type = prime vs. target; default reference level = prime (when present)
# Prime Visibility = masked vs. visible; default reference level = masked
# Trial Type = critical vs. probe; default reference level = critical
# Group = DLD vs. TL; default reference level = DLD
# For gender, female = -0.5 (after centering), male = 0.5 (after centering)
# Detailed Language Status = language status + bilingual type (see below); default reference level= English monolingual
# Language Status = English monolingual vs. English primary; default reference level (set above) \ = English monolingual
# For language status, English monolingual = -0.5 (after centering), English primary/bilingual = 0.5 (after centering)
# Bilingual Type = sequential vs. simultaneous and the languages spoken; default reference level = NA? sequential bilingual (English-French)?
# For handedness, L = -0.5 (after centering), R = 0.5 (after centering)
# PVT = prime visibility threshold (shortest prime duration at which participant identified > 50% of animal primes presented at that duration); 50 vs. 67 vs. 83 vs. 100 vs. > 117; default reference level (set above) = 50
```



## Descriptives
```{r}
# N400 mean amplitudes by group, priming condition, experimental condition, and prime visibility (collapsed across region and hemisphere)
crittarg_data_grouped1 <- group_by(crittarg_data, Experimental.Condition, Group, Prime.Visibility, Priming, ISI)
summarise(crittarg_data_grouped1, # summarize operation by group
  mean = mean(Mean.Amp),
  std = sd(Mean.Amp)
    )

# N400 mean amplitudes by group, priming condition, experimental condition, and prime visibility
crittarg_data_grouped2 <- group_by(crittarg_data, Experimental.Condition, Group, Prime.Visibility, Priming, ISI, Region, Hemisphere)
summarise(crittarg_data_grouped2, # summarize operation by group
  mean = mean(Mean.Amp),
  std = sd(Mean.Amp)
    )
```

## Analyses
### Finding the maximal convergent model (Prime*ISI*Region*Hemisphere)
#### DLD data
##### Masked Word Data
FINAL BASE MODEL: DLDmaskedwordm4 <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming*ISI*Region*Hemisphere + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=dldmaskedword_data
```{r}
DLDmaskedwordm1 <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming*ISI*Region*Hemisphere + (1|Participant.ID)+ (1|Channel), data=dldmaskedword_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6))) # isSingular warning, so checking random effects' variances
summary(rePCA(DLDmaskedwordm1)) # PCA results indicate no variability in the random effects for Channel, so trying a model with that random effect removed

DLDmaskedwordm2 <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming*ISI*Region*Hemisphere + (1|Participant.ID), data=dldmaskedword_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6))) # converges! now building random effects

DLDmaskedwordm3 <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming*ISI*Region*Hemisphere + (1+Priming|Participant.ID), data=dldmaskedword_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6))) # converges! comparing models to ensure this model has the better fit of the two
anova(DLDmaskedwordm3,DLDmaskedwordm2) # the smaller/lower the AIC and/or BIC value, the “better” is the predictive performance of the model; a very small p-value (< .001) means that adding the additional IVs to the model leads to a significantly improved fit over the reduced model --> significant: prefer DLDmaskedwordm3 over DLDmaskedwordm2; continuing to build random effects

DLDmaskedwordm4 <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming*ISI*Region*Hemisphere + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=dldmaskedword_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6))) # converges! comparing models to ensure this model has the better fit of the two
anova(DLDmaskedwordm3,DLDmaskedwordm4) # the smaller/lower the AIC and/or BIC value, the “better” is the predictive performance of the model; a very small p-value (< .001) means that adding the additional IVs to the model leads to a significantly improved fit over the reduced model --> significant: prefer DLDmaskedwordm4 over DLDmaskedwordm3; now to test the covariates!
```
##### Masked Picture Data

### Evaluating lmers (Prime*ISI*Region*Hemisphere)
#### DLD data
##### Masked Word Data
Results:
- significant fixed effects:
  - priming x region (p = .034)
  - priming x ISI x region (p = .018)
- significant simple effects:
  - nothing when corrected for multiple comparisons (regional differences probably explain the significant interactions with region)
  - based on uncorrected p-values, significant interaction of priming x ISI in parietal region (p = .034) 

##### Masked Picture Data
Results:
- significant fixed effects:
  - priming x ISI (p = 0.001)
  - priming x region (p = .035)
  - priming x ISI x hemisphere (p = .019)
  - priming x ISI x region (p = .002)
- significant simple effects:
  - significant interaction of priming x ISI in occipital region (even when corrected for multiple comparisons) (p = .005)
  - based on uncorrected p-values, significant interaction of priming x ISI in parietal region (p = .038)
  - significant interaction of priming x ISI in left hemisphere (even when corrected for multiple comparisons) (p = .005)
  - significant effect of priming in central region (even when corrected for multiple comparisons) (p = .008)
  - significant effect of priming in 67-ms ISI (even when corrected for multiple comparisons)! (p < .0001)

##### Masked Word Data
Results:
- significant fixed effects:
  - priming x region (p < .001)
  - priming x ISI x region (p < .001)
  - priming x ISI x hemisphere x region (p < .001)
- significant simple effects:
  - significant effect of priming in frontal region (even when corrected for multiple comparisons) (p = .004)
  - significant effect of priming in occipital region (even when corrected for multiple comparisons) (p < .001)
  - based on uncorrected p-values, significant effect of priming in central region (p = .013)
  - (regional differences probably explain most of the other significant interactions with region)
```{r}
#############################################################
### ALL THE MODELS TO TEST THE FIXED EFFECTS OF INTEREST ###
#############################################################
DLDvispic.noints <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming+ISI+Region+Hemisphere + (1+ISI|Participant.ID), data=dldvispic_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

DLDvispic.nopriming <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ ISI+Region+Hemisphere + (1+ISI|Participant.ID), data=dldvispic_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

DLDvispic.primingxisixhemi <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming*ISI*Hemisphere+Region + (1+ISI|Participant.ID), data=dldvispic_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

########################################################################
### ALL THE MODEL COMPARISONS TO TEST THE FIXED EFFECTS OF INTEREST ###
########################################################################
# the smaller/lower the AIC and/or BIC value, the “better” is the predictive performance of the model; a very small p-value (< .001) means that adding the additional IVs to the model leads to a significantly improved fit over the reduced model --> not significant: prefer reduced model over augmented model / significant: prefer augmented model over reduced model

# priming - not significant
anova(DLDvispic.noints,DLDvispic.nopriming)

# priming x ISI - not significant
anova(DLDvispic.noints,DLDvispic.primingxisi)

# priming x hemisphere - not significant
anova(DLDvispic.noints,DLDvispic.primingxhemi)

# priming x region - significant! (p < .001)
anova(DLDvispic.noints,DLDvispic.primingxreg)

# priming x ISI x hemisphere - not significant
anova(DLDvispic.noints,DLDvispic.primingxisixhemi)

# priming x ISI x region - significant! (p < .001)
anova(DLDvispic.noints,DLDvispic.primingxisixregion)

# priming x ISI x hemisphere x region - significant! (p < .001)
anova(DLDvispic.noints,DLDvispic.allints)
```

  - priming x ISI x hemisphere x region (p < .001)

##### Visible Word Data
Results:
- significant fixed effects:
  - priming x region  (p < .001)
  - priming x ISI x region  (p < .001)
  - priming x ISI x hemisphere x region  (p < .001)
- significant simple effects:
  - significant priming effect in central region (even when corrected for multiple comparisons) (p < .001)
  - significant priming effect in occipital region (even when corrected for multiple comparisons) (p = .001)
  - based on uncorrected p-values, significant priming effect in frontal region (p = .013)
```{r}
#############################################################
### ALL THE MODELS TO TEST THE FIXED EFFECTS OF INTEREST ###
#############################################################
TLvisword.noints <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming+ISI+Region+Hemisphere + lang.stat.c  +  wrmt.c + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=tlvisword_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

TLvisword.nopriming <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ ISI+Region+Hemisphere + lang.stat.c  +  wrmt.c + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=tlvisword_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

#TLvisword.noisi <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming+Region+Hemisphere + lang.stat.c  +  wrmt.c + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=tlvisword_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

TLvisword.primingxisi <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming*ISI+Region+Hemisphere + lang.stat.c  +  wrmt.c + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=tlvisword_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

TLvisword.primingxhemi <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming*Hemisphere+ISI+Region + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=tlvisword_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

TLvisword.primingxreg <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming*Region+ISI+Hemisphere + lang.stat.c  +  wrmt.c + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=tlvisword_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

TLvisword.primingxisixhemi <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming*ISI*Hemisphere+Region + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=tlvisword_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

TLvisword.primingxisixregion <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming*ISI*Region+Hemisphere + lang.stat.c  +  wrmt.c + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=tlvisword_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

TLvisword.allints <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming*ISI*Region*Hemisphere + lang.stat.c  +  wrmt.c + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=tlvisword_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

########################################################################
### ALL THE MODEL COMPARISONS TO TEST THE FIXED EFFECTS OF INTEREST ###
########################################################################
# the smaller/lower the AIC and/or BIC value, the “better” is the predictive performance of the model; a very small p-value (< .001) means that adding the additional IVs to the model leads to a significantly improved fit over the reduced model --> not significant: prefer reduced model over augmented model / significant: prefer augmented model over reduced model

# priming - not significant
anova(TLvisword.noints,TLvisword.nopriming)

# priming x ISI - not significant
anova(TLvisword.noints,TLvisword.primingxisi)

# priming x hemisphere - not significant
anova(TLvisword.noints,TLvisword.primingxhemi)

# priming x region - significant! (p < .001)
anova(TLvisword.noints,TLvisword.primingxreg)

# priming x ISI x hemisphere - not significant
anova(TLvisword.noints,TLvisword.primingxisixhemi)

# priming x ISI x region - significant! (p < .001)
anova(TLvisword.noints,TLvisword.primingxisixregion)

# priming x ISI x hemisphere x region - significant! (p < .001)
anova(TLvisword.noints,TLvisword.allints)
```

##### Visible Picture Data
Results:
- significant fixed effects:
  - priming (p = .013)
  - priming x region (p < .001)
  - priming x ISI x region (p < .001)
  - priming x ISI x hemisphere x region (p < .001)
- significant simple effects:
  - significant effect of priming in frontal region (even when corrected form multiple comparisons) (p < .001)
  - significant effect of priming in central region (even when corrected form multiple comparisons) (p < .001)
  - significant effect of priming in occipital region (even when corrected form multiple comparisons) (p < .001)
```{r}
#############################################################
### ALL THE MODELS TO TEST THE FIXED EFFECTS OF INTEREST ###
#############################################################
TLvispic.noints <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming+ISI+Region+Hemisphere + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=tlvispic_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

TLvispic.nopriming <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ ISI+Region+Hemisphere + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=tlvispic_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

#TLvispic.noisi <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming+Region+Hemisphere + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=tlvispic_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

TLvispic.primingxisi <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming*ISI+Region+Hemisphere + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=tlvispic_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

TLvispic.primingxhemi <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming*Hemisphere+ISI+Region + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=tlvispic_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

TLvispic.primingxreg <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming*Region+ISI+Hemisphere + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=tlvispic_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

TLvispic.primingxisixhemi <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming*ISI*Hemisphere+Region + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=tlvispic_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

TLvispic.primingxisixregion <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming*ISI*Region+Hemisphere + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=tlvispic_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

TLvispic.allints <- lmer(Mean.Amp ~ Priming*ISI*Region*Hemisphere + (1+Priming*ISI|Participant.ID), data=tlvispic_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6)))

########################################################################
### ALL THE MODEL COMPARISONS TO TEST THE FIXED EFFECTS OF INTEREST ###
########################################################################
# the smaller/lower the AIC and/or BIC value, the “better” is the predictive performance of the model; a very small p-value (< .001) means that adding the additional IVs to the model leads to a significantly improved fit over the reduced model --> not significant: prefer reduced model over augmented model / significant: prefer augmented model over reduced model

# priming - significant! (p = .013)
anova(TLvispic.noints,TLvispic.nopriming)

# priming x ISI - not significant
anova(TLvispic.noints,TLvispic.primingxisi)

# priming x hemisphere - not significant
anova(TLvispic.noints,TLvispic.primingxhemi)

# priming x region - significant! (p < .001)
anova(TLvispic.noints,TLvispic.primingxreg)

# priming x ISI x hemisphere - not significant
anova(TLvispic.noints,TLvispic.primingxisixhemi)

# priming x ISI x region - significant! (p < .001)
anova(TLvispic.noints,TLvispic.primingxisixregion)

# priming x ISI x hemisphere x region - significant! (p < .001)
anova(TLvispic.noints,TLvispic.allints)
```

# All Diff Score Data

## Data Manipulation
```{r}
# Load data (1 data frame)
diffscore_data <- read.csv(here("PADLD Data", "PADLD Diff Scores Data.csv"),stringsAsFactors=TRUE) # N400 priming effect difference scores

diffscore_data %<>%
  mutate(Priming.Diff.Score = as.numeric(Priming.Diff.Score),
         Channel = factor(Channel),
         Region = factor(Region, levels=c("frontal","central","parietal","occipital")),
         Hemisphere = factor(Hemisphere, levels=c("left","midline","right")),
         Experimental.Condition = factor(Experimental.Condition),
         Prime.Visibility = factor (Prime.Visibility),
         Group = factor(Group), 
         gender.c = as.numeric(Gender) - 1.5,
         Detailed.Language.Status = factor(Detailed.Language.Status),
         Language.Status = factor(Language.Status,levels=c("English monolingual","English primary")),
         lang.stat.c = as.numeric(Language.Status) - 1.5,
         Bilingual.Type = factor(Bilingual.Type),
         celf5 = as.numeric(CELF5.CLS),
         celf5.c = as.numeric(scale(CELF5.CLS, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)),
         age.c = as.numeric(scale(Average.Age, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)),
         nwr.ppc.arc = asin(sqrt(as.numeric(NWR.PPC)/100)),
         nwr.ppc.arc.c = as.numeric(scale(nwr.ppc.arc, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)),
         nwr.pcc.arc = asin(sqrt(as.numeric(NWR.PCC)/100)),
         nwr.pcc.arc.c = as.numeric(scale(nwr.pcc.arc, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)),
         tills= as.numeric(TILLS.VA.Standard.Score),
         tills.c = as.numeric(scale(TILLS.VA.Standard.Score, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)),
         toni= as.numeric(TONI.Deviation.Quotient),
         toni.c = as.numeric(scale(TONI.Deviation.Quotient, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)),
         wrmt = as.numeric(WRMT.LWI.Standard.Score),
         wrmt.c = as.numeric(scale(WRMT.LWI.Standard.Score, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)),
         flanker = as.numeric(Flanker.Standard.Score),
         flanker.c = as.numeric(scale(Flanker.Standard.Score, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)),
         handedness = factor(Handedness),
         hand.c = as.numeric(handedness) - 1.5,
         pvt = factor(PVT,levels=c("50","67","83","100","> 117")))
str(diffscore_data)

# Create some data subsets
masked_diffscore_data <- subset(diffscore_data, Prime.Visibility == "masked")
vis_diffscore_data <- subset(diffscore_data, Prime.Visibility == "visible")

# Notes:
# Region = anteriority/posteriority; default reference level (set above) = frontal
# Hemisphere = laterality; default reference level (set above) = left
# Experimental Condition = picture vs. word; default reference level = picture
# Prime Visibility = masked vs. visible; default reference level = masked
# Group = DLD vs. TL; default reference level = DLD
# For gender, female = -0.5 (after centering), male = 0.5 (after centering)
# Detailed Language Status = language status + bilingual type (see below); default reference level= English monolingual
# Language Status = English monolingual vs. English primary; default reference level (set above) \ = English monolingual
# For language status, English monolingual = -0.5 (after centering), English primary/bilingual = 0.5 (after centering)
# Bilingual Type = sequential vs. simultaneous and the languages spoken; default reference level = NA? sequential bilingual (English-French)?
# For handedness, L = -0.5 (after centering), R = 0.5 (after centering)
# PVT = prime visibility threshold (shortest prime duration at which participant identified > 50% of animal primes presented at that duration); 50 vs. 67 vs. 83 vs. 100 vs. > 117; default reference level (set above) = 50
```

## Analyses
### Finding the maximal convergent model
#### Masked Data
FINAL BASE MODELS: 
diffscoresmaskedm3 <- lm(tills ~ Priming.Diff.Score*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere, data=masked_diffscore_data)
diffscoresmaskedm6 <- lmer(Priming.Diff.Score ~ tills.c*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere + (1+Experimental.Condition|Participant.ID) , data=masked_diffscore_data
```{r}
diffscoresmaskedm1 <- lmer(tills ~ Priming.Diff.Score*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere + (1|Participant.ID)+ (1|Channel), data=masked_diffscore_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6))) # isSingular warning, so checking random effects' variances
summary(rePCA(diffscoresmaskedm1)) # PCA results indicate no variability in the random effects for Channel, so trying a model with that random effect removed

diffscoresmaskedm2 <- lmer(tills ~ Priming.Diff.Score*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere + (1|Participant.ID), data=masked_diffscore_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6))) # model failed to converge, so checking random effects' variances
summary(rePCA(diffscoresmaskedm2)) # PCA results an extremely large SD for the random intercept of Participant ID, so trying removing random effects altogether

diffscoresmaskedm3 <- lm(tills ~ Priming.Diff.Score*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere, data=masked_diffscore_data) # converges! now to test covariates

diffscoresmaskedm4 <- lmer(Priming.Diff.Score ~ tills.c*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere + (1|Participant.ID) + (1|Channel) , data=masked_diffscore_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6))) # isSingular warning and failed to converge, so checking random effects' variances
summary(rePCA(diffscoresmaskedwordm4)) # PCA results indicate close to no variability in the random effects for Channel, so trying a model with that random effect removed

diffscoresmaskedm5 <- lmer(Priming.Diff.Score ~ tills.c*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere + (1|Participant.ID) , data=masked_diffscore_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6))) # converges! now to build random effects

diffscoresmaskedm6 <- lmer(Priming.Diff.Score ~ tills.c*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere + (1+tills.c|Participant.ID) , data=masked_diffscore_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6))) # isSingular warning; continuing to build random effects structure

diffscoresmaskedm6 <- lmer(Priming.Diff.Score ~ tills.c*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere + (1+Experimental.Condition|Participant.ID) , data=masked_diffscore_data, REML=FALSE,control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=1e6))) # converges! now to test covariates

```

### Testing impact of covariates
#### Masked Data
##### TILLS as DV
FINAL MODEL:diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc.toni.wrmt.handedness.pvt <- lm(tills ~ Priming.Diff.Score*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere+ gender.c + age.c + lang.stat.c + celf5.c + nwr.ppc.arc.c + toni.c + wrmt.c +  hand.c  +  pvt , data=masked_diffscore_data)
```{r}
diffscoresmaskedm3.gender <- lm(tills ~ Priming.Diff.Score*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere + gender.c , data=masked_diffscore_data) # to determine whether gender significantly improves model fit
anova(diffscoresmaskedm3,diffscoresmaskedm3.gender)# the smaller/lower the AIC and/or BIC value, the “better” is the predictive performance of the model; a very small p-value (< .001) means that adding the additional IVs to the model leads to a significantly improved fit over the reduced model --> significant: prefer diffscoresmaskedm3.gender over diffscoresmaskedm3

diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age <- lm(tills ~ Priming.Diff.Score*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere + gender.c  +age.c , data=masked_diffscore_data) # to determine whether age significantly improves model fit
anova(diffscoresmaskedm3.gender,diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age) # the smaller/lower the AIC and/or BIC value, the “better” is the predictive performance of the model; a very small p-value (< .001) means that adding the additional IVs to the model leads to a significantly improved fit over the reduced model -->significant: prefer diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age over diffscoresmaskedm3.gender

diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat <- lm(tills ~ Priming.Diff.Score*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere  + gender.c + age.c  + lang.stat.c , data=masked_diffscore_data) # to determine whether language status significantly improves model fit
anova(diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age, diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat) # the smaller/lower the AIC and/or BIC value, the “better” is the predictive performance of the model; a very small p-value (< .001) means that adding the additional IVs to the model leads to a significantly improved fit over the reduced model --> significant: prefer diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat over diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age

diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf <- lm(tills ~ Priming.Diff.Score*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere  + gender.c + age.c + lang.stat.c  + celf5.c , data=masked_diffscore_data) # to determine whether CELF-5 CLS significantly improves model fit
anova(diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat,diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf) # the smaller/lower the AIC and/or BIC value, the “better” is the predictive performance of the model; a very small p-value (< .001) means that adding the additional IVs to the model leads to a significantly improved fit over the reduced model --> significant: prefer diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf over diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat

diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc <- lm(tills ~ Priming.Diff.Score*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere + gender.c + age.c + lang.stat.c + celf5.c  + nwr.ppc.arc.c , data=masked_diffscore_data) # to determine whether NWR PPC significantly improves model fit
anova(diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf,diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc) # the smaller/lower the AIC and/or BIC value, the “better” is the predictive performance of the model; a very small p-value (< .001) means that adding the additional IVs to the model leads to a significantly improved fit over the reduced model --> significant: prefer diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc over diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf

diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrpcc <- lm(tills ~ Priming.Diff.Score*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere+ gender.c + age.c + lang.stat.c + celf5.c  +  nwr.pcc.arc.c , data=masked_diffscore_data) # to determine whether NWR PCC significantly improves model fit
anova(diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf,diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrpcc) # the smaller/lower the AIC and/or BIC value, the “better” is the predictive performance of the model; a very small p-value (< .001) means that adding the additional IVs to the model leads to a significantly improved fit over the reduced model --> not significant: prefer diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrpcc over diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf; comparing models to see whether including nwrppc or nwrpcc leads to a better fitting model

anova(diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc,diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrpcc) # the smaller/lower the AIC and/or BIC value, the “better” is the predictive performance of the model; a very small p-value (< .001) means that adding the additional IVs to the model leads to a significantly improved fit over the reduced model --> not significant: prefer diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc over diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc

diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc.toni <- lm(tills ~ Priming.Diff.Score*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere+ gender.c + age.c + lang.stat.c + celf5.c + nwr.ppc.arc.c  +  toni.c , data=masked_diffscore_data) # to determine whether TONI Deviation Quotient significantly improves model fit
anova(diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc,diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc.toni) # the smaller/lower the AIC and/or BIC value, the “better” is the predictive performance of the model; a very small p-value (< .001) means that adding the additional IVs to the model leads to a significantly improved fit over the reduced model --> significant: prefer diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc.toni over diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc

diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc.toni.wrmt <- lm(tills ~ Priming.Diff.Score*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere+ gender.c + age.c + lang.stat.c + celf5.c + nwr.ppc.arc.c + toni.c  +  wrmt.c , data=masked_diffscore_data) # to determine whether WRMT LWI Standard Score significantly improves model fit
anova(diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc.toni,diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc.toni.wrmt) # the smaller/lower the AIC and/or BIC value, the “better” is the predictive performance of the model; a very small p-value (< .001) means that adding the additional IVs to the model leads to a significantly improved fit over the reduced model --> significant: prefer diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc.toni.wrmt over diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc.toni

diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc.toni.wrmt.flanker <- lm(tills ~ Priming.Diff.Score*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere+ gender.c + age.c + lang.stat.c + celf5.c + nwr.ppc.arc.c + toni.c + wrmt.c  +  flanker.c , data=masked_diffscore_data) # to determine whether Flanker Standard Score significantly improves model fit
anova(diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc.toni.wrmt, diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc.toni.wrmt.flanker) # the smaller/lower the AIC and/or BIC value, the “better” is the predictive performance of the model; a very small p-value (< .001) means that adding the additional IVs to the model leads to a significantly improved fit over the reduced model --> not significant: prefer diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc.toni.wrmt over diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc.toni.wrmt.flanker

diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc.toni.wrmt.handedness <- lm(tills ~ Priming.Diff.Score*Experimental.Condition*Region*Hemisphere+ gender.c + age.c + lang.stat.c + celf5.c + nwr.ppc.arc.c + toni.c + wrmt.c  +  hand.c , data=masked_diffscore_data) # to determine whether handedness significantly improves model fit
anova(diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc.toni.wrmt,diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc.toni.wrmt.handedness) # the smaller/lower the AIC and/or BIC value, the “better” is the predictive performance of the model; a very small p-value (< .001) means that adding the additional IVs to the model leads to a significantly improved fit over the reduced model --> significant: prefer diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc.toni.wrmt.handedness over diffscoresmaskedm3.gender.age.langstat.celf.nwrppc.toni.wrmt
```

#### Correlations
Results: 
- TILLS Vocabulary Awareness standard scores and N400 priming effect difference scores are not significantly correlated for masked word or masked picture data
```{r}
maskedword_diffscore_data <- subset(diffscore_data, Prime.Visibility == "masked" & Experimental.Condition == "word")
maskedpic_diffscore_data <- subset(diffscore_data, Prime.Visibility == "masked" & Experimental.Condition == "picture")

target_vars = c("Priming.Diff.Score","tills")

cor(maskedword_diffscore_data[,target_vars], method = "pearson", use="complete.obs")
wordp_values <- rcorr(as.matrix(maskedword_diffscore_data[,target_vars]))
print(wordp_values)

cor(maskedpic_diffscore_data[,target_vars], method = "pearson", use="complete.obs")
picp_values <- rcorr(as.matrix(maskedpic_diffscore_data[,target_vars]))
print(picp_values)
```
